references.text: Aaron and his sons were to wash themselves with water at the entrance of the tent of meeting as part of the consecration ritual for the priesthood.
The priests had to wash their hands and feet with water from the bronze basin before entering the tent of meeting or approaching the altar.
Moses was commanded to bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting, wash them with water, and clothe them in the holy garments.
Moses washed Aaron and his sons with water as part of their priestly consecration.
Aaron was to wash his body with water before putting on the holy linen garments on the Day of Atonement.
Aaron was to enter the tent of meeting, take off the linen garments he had worn when entering the Most Holy Place.
Aaron was to offer a burnt offering and make atonement for himself and for the people.
Aaron offered a burnt offering for himself and the people according to the Lord's command.
The priest was to wash his clothes and bathe his body with water as part of the purification ritual.
A prophetic promise that the Lord will sprinkle clean water on His people and cleanse them from all impurity.
The high priest entered the Most Holy Place once a year with blood to make atonement for himself and the sins of the people.
Believers are encouraged to draw near to God with their bodies washed in clean water, pointing back to the priests' purification rituals.
